Looking for games that were great at the time, but aren't anymore. This could be for a number of reasons, maybe it was a more primitive version of something much better that we have now or maybe it was using some gimmick which would be impressive back then but isn't now, etc.

Games you have to have played as a kid in order to enjoy also count here.
What are some games that did not hold up well?

I find that the original Legend of Zelda on the NES hasn't held up well. Sure, it is a fun game. It's challenging and exciting, but it is way too cryptic. What little hints you get are very vague, and finding out what part of the level has a hidden bomb-able cave is very hit-or-miss. It's just one of those games that you need to have played as a kid to truly be able to enjoy, when it was fresh and most people hadn't seen anything quite like it before.

Another thing is that it would be one of those games, where groups of friends would look for things within the game and share the information with each other(unless someone had a guide). With the internet, it feels like that part is ruined too. People will just look things up on the internet and you might as well be following a guide telling you the best route through the game.

It's a shame, because it's a game I would love to enjoy playing and which could be really fun, had I grown up with it. I didn't, and thus, it doesn't really hold up enough for me to enjoy it.

I never really thought about The Legend of Zelda not holding up, but I agree with you. I just played it so much as a kid that it still feels natural to me. The more NES games I've been playing recently, the more I find many being too cryptic like this.

I'm wondering if cryptic/secretive game designs were intentional so they could sell more copies of Nintendo Power and more calls to their tip hotline.

It certainly was intentional, I remember hearing somewhere that Miyamoto(The game's designer) was urged by others at Nintendo to make things less cryptic, but he kept it. Not sure where I heard this though, and I can't find any sources for that, so take it with a grain of salt.

Even without that, it's pretty safe to say it was intentional. It's highly unlikely they didn't playtest the game, so there's no way they couldn't have noticed how cryptic the game was.

It's a bit like Metroid, which is of similar nature. It's designed so you get lost, and doesn't give you a map. It was also developed at Nintendo internally, so they probably had that in mind when designing these games. Not impossible to figure out, but hard enough to make buying a guide very tempting.

Super Mario 64. It blew me away at the time, but playing it recently the graphics feels flat and the camera is a constant battle.

I played hundreds of hours of it as a kid, but as an adult it just feels like a glorified tech demo.
Super Mario 64 was a huge pioneer in 3D third person gameplay, but I just can't go back and replay it like I do Super Mario World and Super Mario 2 and 3. There is definitely something missing.

Demon's Crest is a big one for me. It gets a lot of hype, and the basic mechanics and platforming are great, but having to visit the same areas over and over really gets old. Plus not knowing where the hell to go is irritating.
